answer.text: Maridebart cafraglutide and Semaglutide are both in late-stage obesity development, but differ in trial maturity, geographic reach, and clinical context exploration. Maridebart cafraglutide's program is newer (first Phase 3 trials initiated in 2023) with a strong focus on Japan and switching from other GLP-1RAs, while Semaglutide has a broader, more established global footprint with extensive Phase 3 data across diverse obesity populations including those with pre-diabetes, type 2 diabetes, and East Asian subgroups.

key_findings.text: Maridebart cafraglutide has 8 trials (7 active) with 6 Phase 3 studies, all initiated between 2023-2026, focusing on obesity/overweight populations with enrollment medians of 771 versus Semaglutide's 26 trials (2 active) with 25 Phase 3 studies initiated 2015-2026 and median enrollment of 407.

Maridebart cafraglutide trials emphasize Japan (4/8 trials) and switching from other GLP-1RAs (MARITIME-SWITCH), while Semaglutide has broad global coverage including dedicated East Asian trials (NCT05132088) and trials in participants with obesity plus type 2 diabetes (NCT03552757).

Both programs evaluate percent change in body weight and >=5% weight loss, but Semaglutide trials more frequently incorporate health-related quality of life measures (SF-36, IWQOL-Lite) and glycaemic status analyses.

RETRIEVED_EVIDENCE.brief_summary:
Novo Nordisk are doing this study to see if semaglutide tablets can be used as a treatment to help people living with overweight or obesity lose weight.

This study will look at the change in participants' body weight. Participants will either get semaglutide tablets (new medicine) or placebo tablets ('dummy' medicine that looks like semaglutide but has no effect on the body). For a fair comparison, people are divided into two groups at random by a computer. This process is called randomisation.

Semaglutide tablets are new medicine being tested to treat overweight and obesity. Doctors in many countries can already prescribe semaglutide tablets at lower doses to treat type 2 diabetes.

Participants will get semaglutide or placebo tablets for 68 weeks and will need to take 1 tablet every morning.

In addition to taking the medicine, participants will have talks with study staff about:

* healthy food choices
* how to be more physically active
* what participants can do to lose weight The study will last for about 1½ year. Participants will have 14 clinic visits and 7 phone calls with the study healthcare professional.

Blood samples will be taken at 12 visits. Women cannot take part if pregnant, breast-feeding or planning to get pregnant during the study period. If participants are a woman and are able to become pregnant, participants will be checked for pregnancy via urine tests.

answer.text: Eli Lilly's Orforglipron and Novo Nordisk's CagriSema differ in development scale and trial objectives, with Orforglipron having a smaller, more focused development program targeting oral administration in adults and adolescents, while CagriSema has a larger, more diverse program including pediatric studies and long-term weight maintenance evaluations.

Orforglipron trials emphasize weight reduction and maintenance in participants transitioning from tirzepatide or semaglutide, with specific studies in Japanese populations and adolescents.
CagriSema trials include comparative studies against placebo and other agents, pediatric evaluations, and long-term extensions examining sustained weight loss and health outcomes.
